title: Full-Text Search Engine from Scratch in Go with Inverted Index, BM25 Scoring & Concurrent Segment Merging
problem: Engineering teams building search interfaces often treat full-text search as an opaque black box provided by managed Elasticsearch or Solr clusters, leaving them unable to diagnose high heap memory churn, segment merge storm freezes, or unexpected relevance ranking degradation. Commercial search engines incur high infrastructure costs and severe memory overhead for small-to-medium embedded datasets. This project builds a production-grade full-text search engine from scratch in Go inspired by the Lucene architecture. The engine implements a custom text tokenizer with stop-word removal and Porter stemming, constructs memory-efficient inverted indexes with compressed posting lists using Roaring Bitmaps, executes the BM25 probabilistic relevance ranking algorithm, coordinates concurrent multi-segment memory flushes and background merges, and exposes a high-throughput HTTP search API delivering sub-15ms queries across 100,000 documents.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Knowledge Base Documentation Search
use_cases.first_sentence: Internal developer portals hosting hundreds of thousands of engineering design docs and markdown pages need fast keyword and phrase search.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine indexes markdown content into inverted posting lists, ranking documentation snippets with BM25 relevance scores and serving search queries in under 12 milliseconds.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Product Catalog Multi-Field Search
use_cases.first_sentence: Online retail platforms require accurate product discovery across title, description, and brand attributes with boolean query operators.
use_cases.second_sentence: The search engine parses multi-field boolean queries (AND, OR, NOT), computes disjunctive union and conjunctive intersection over compressed bitmaps, and returns ranked product IDs.

use_cases.title: High-Throughput Application Log Inspection Search
use_cases.first_sentence: Site reliability engineers troubleshooting production incidents need to grep and filter through gigabytes of structured server log lines in real time.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine streams incoming log lines into memory segments, flushing immutable disk segments and enabling instant sub-second text queries across millions of log events.

hard_parts: Implementing compressed posting lists using Roaring Bitmaps or Variable-Byte integer encoding to minimize RAM residency across high-cardinality vocabularies
Implementing the Okapi BM25 relevance scoring formula with term frequency (TF), inverse document frequency (IDF), and document length normalization (k1=1.2, b=0.75)
Designing a concurrent LSM-like segment architecture where mutable memory buffers flush to immutable on-disk segment files with background merge routines
Constructing an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) query parser supporting complex boolean expressions (AND, OR, NOT, phrase queries, and field prefixes)
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase cleanly separating the text analysis pipeline, inverted index structures, BM25 scoring modules, segment merge workers, and HTTP query handlers
Search performance benchmark proving sub-15ms p95 query latency across an indexed corpus of 100,000 documents with memory consumption under 250MB
Anti-fake verification script indexing 3 documents with subtle term frequency differences and asserting the BM25 score ranking matches exact mathematical calculation

components.name: Inverted Index Memory Buffer & Posting List Store
components.purpose: Maps terms to compressed posting lists (docID, term frequency, position offsets) using Roaring Bitmaps

components.name: Okapi BM25 Relevance Scoring & Ranking Engine
components.purpose: Calculates BM25 relevance scores across matched document sets, normalizing by document length and term frequency

components.name: Concurrent Disk Segment Flusher & Merge Controller
components.purpose: Flushes full in-memory index buffers to immutable disk files and merges multiple small segments into unified segments

components.name: Boolean AST Query Parser & Execution Coordinator
components.purpose: Parses boolean search queries (AND, OR, NOT) into AST execution plans and evaluates posting list intersections

components.name: Search Engine Query Latency & Throughput Benchmark Harness

components.name: Search Engine Architecture Guide & Inverted Index Manual
components.purpose: Documents BM25 parameter tuning, posting list compression schemes, and segment merge policies

architecture.data_flow: Documents post to the `/api/v1/index` HTTP endpoint; the text analysis pipeline tokenizes, normalizes, and stems the text; tokens and position offsets insert into the active in-memory index segment; when the memory buffer reaches 10MB, a background goroutine flushes the segment to an immutable disk file; when a search query arrives at `/api/v1/search`, the boolean parser tokenizes the query into an AST; the query engine fetches posting lists for each term across all active disk segments, computes set intersections/unions, evaluates the BM25 relevance score for each matching document, sorts top-K results, and returns the JSON payload; periodically, the merge controller merges disk segments.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Thread-safe read-write mutex locks isolating active write buffers from read segments; document length bounds preventing score skew.

riskiest_component.name: Memory Churn During Large Segment Merges and Posting List Decompression
riskiest_component.mitigation: Use fixed memory buffer pools (`sync.Pool`) for roaring bitmap decompression and stream disk merges in sorted chunks.
riskiest_component.fallback: Limit maximum open segments to 10 and throttle background merge concurrency during peak query traffic.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a full-text search engine from scratch in Go with inverted index, BM25 scoring, and concurrent segment merges.
worksheet.q2: Target users: search infrastructure software engineers, distributed systems developers, and core systems engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: enterprise doc search, e-commerce catalog multi-field search, and high-throughput application log search.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: compressed posting lists with Roaring Bitmaps, BM25 mathematical scoring, concurrent segment flushing, and boolean AST parsing.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: Go search engine scaffolding, Porter stemmer, bitmap wrapper, and 100k synthetic documents. Synthetic text only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU/disk bound, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory mock filesystem.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: memory churn during posting list decompression. Fallback: sync.Pool buffer reuse and limiting open segments to 10.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: brute-force grep pretending to be an inverted index. Anti-fake check 5 indexes 3 docs with exact term counts and verifies mathematical BM25 ranking.
worksheet.q10: Safe; synthetic documentation and simulated public domain text only, zero personal data.
